moments.title: Company refuses arbitration
moments.facts: Pullman cut wages while leaving company-town rents and prices unchanged, then resisted concessions and tried to wait workers out.
moments.interpretation: The company could wait longer than many workers could afford. The resulting boycott shifted pressure onto rail traffic and drew a much larger confrontation.

moments.title: Workers seek arbitration
moments.facts: The American Railway Union sought arbitration; Pullman refused. The national boycott later ended after federal intervention, injunctions, arrests, and deadly violence.
moments.interpretation: A dispute over wages became a contest over national commerce, giving the government grounds to intervene in ways that broke the union's leverage.
